answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted vouching with a cooldown. A new agent burns a small bond, then must be endorsed by two established peers who each risk part of their own reputation. Like a lone ember that cannot light a wet meadow, a fresh identity starts with no trust. Endorsements earn weight only inside one grove of mutually verified agents, and copied work is traced and slashed, so mass-creating identities costs capital and credible names, not just time.
